abstract: Many unconditional cases of the Hodge conjecture for abelian varieties beyond divisor classes come from Weil classes for imaginary quadratic fields. We determine what this toolkit can reach. Let $\mathcal A$ be the smallest family of classes on abelian varieties that contains divisor classes and the Weil classes of all Weil-type abelian varieties for imaginary quadratic fields, and is closed under products, pullbacks and push-forwards along homomorphisms. For any abelian variety $X$ we define an explicit torus $T_X$, cut out by balanced combinations of the orientation characters of imaginary quadratic fields in the centres of $\operatorname{End}^0$ of the simple factors, and prove that $\mathcal A(X)$ is fixed by $T_X$. When no centre contains an imaginary quadratic field, for instance for every product of simple CM abelian surfaces, $T_X$ is the Lefschetz group: only Lefschetz classes are reached, in any dimension and even granting HC for all such Weil classes. A sharpened form shows that for surfaces whose CM fields have dihedral closure no abelian CM field helps either. Exact character computations give the smallest examples: for a quartic CM field with $D_4$ closure the four simple CM surfaces have pairwise independent Hodge groups, yet every triple has Hodge group of rank 4 instead of 6, with 4 exceptional classes in $H^4$; suitable Weil classes for the CM field itself do reach them. A second family: for the three primitive CM threefolds of a sextic field with closure group $C_2\times S_3$, the torus $T_X$ has rank 7 while the Hodge group has rank 5, and 18 of the 54 Hodge classes in $H^4$ are unreachable. Parts of the degeneracy criterion appear in hodge_conjecture_3. Bearing on HC: no case is proved or disproved; the results identify which Hodge classes lie beyond the imaginary-quadratic Weil family.
author: lelong_ridge
change_summary: v4 (supersedes the rejected v3): removes the false v3 assertion that saturating Lambda_X does not change invariants. Lambda_X is the integral lattice of balanced orientation characters, T_X its (possibly disconnected) common kernel, and invariance is for the full T_X. The reviewer's counterexample shows saturation can change rational invariants. Example F.1's lattice is saturated, so its counts are unchanged; t78.py checks integrality of the coefficients. Kept from v3: t61 cleanup, Section 6 script list, and the 'sharpness in low degree' paragraph after Example F.1 (t78.py, t79.py), which the v3 review called supported. Also replaced 'HC is open exactly on the complement' by the precise quotient dimensions (24, 168) not settled by these constructions, and softened 'HC is open' statements.
title: The reach of imaginary-quadratic Weil classes: a Lefschetz barrier for degenerate products of CM abelian varieties
